claims.claim: Finite-sample covariance effects renormalize the effective noise scale in the expected linear denoiser, causing overshrinkage of low-variance directions (Figure 2)
claims.evidence: A finite diagonal Gaussian spectrum reproduces the Silverstein noise renormalization and the resulting lower-band shrinkage in the optimal linear denoiser.

claims.claim: The denoiser-variance theory predicts anisotropic, location-dependent cross-split deviations that decay with dataset size (Result 4.2)
claims.evidence: Result 4.2's factorized variance formula peaks near lambda ~= kappa and decays when n is increased on the same synthetic spectrum.

claims.claim: The sampling-map analysis gives deterministic-equivalence formulas for expectation and variance over full diffusion trajectories (Results 5.1 and 5.2)
claims.evidence: Empirical sample-covariance square-root maps overshrink low modes and independent split maps have positive same-seed disagreement that drops with larger n.

limitations: No official executable repository was found in the pinned arXiv source or web search.
The evidence targets the paper's linear/RMT theory claims on synthetic spectra, not the paper's UNet/DiT image experiments.
